transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Honestly, I’m here because HR at work and my sister keep telling me I’ve gotten too thin. I don’t really see it the same way—I just feel like my suits fit sharper now. But yeah, my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, and they pushed me to come in.
Have you been intentionally limiting your food intake or trying to lose weight, or does the idea of gaining weight worry you more than usual?

Yeah… I guess I am limiting it. Most days it’s just coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar if I’m between sales calls, and then something small at night, like grilled chicken without rice or anything. If I eat a full meal, it feels like I’ve blown the whole day, so I try to keep it controlled.
Do you have a strong fear of gaining weight or becoming fat, even though you’re already underweight?

Yeah. I mean, I don’t like saying it that way, but yes. If the scale is even a pound higher after a client dinner or a weekend out in Miami, I get this panic feeling, like I’m losing control. Then I start thinking right away about how I’m going to cut back the next day.
Would you say that your overall sense of self or how you feel about yourself is strongly connected to your weight or body shape?

Yeah, I’d say it is. Before a meeting or a date, I’ll look in the mirror and I go straight to my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft at all, it really gets in my head. I feel like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak, even if they probably aren’t thinking that.
Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or exercised excessively to control your weight or shape?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t think I do those things, at least not in a regular way. I mostly just try to control what I eat.
Have you ever gone an entire day without eating to control your weight or shape?

Not usually a whole entire day, no. But most days I keep it pretty minimal—coffee in the morning, maybe a protein bar between sales calls, and then something small at night, like grilled chicken without rice. Once I start eating a full meal, it feels like I’ve messed up the whole day.
Do you ever engage in intense exercise or physical activity specifically to burn off calories or control your weight, even if you're tired or not in the mood?

I’m not sure I’d call it intense exercise. I don’t really have a routine where I’m forcing myself to work out to burn things off. If I do anything, it’s more like walking around or staying busy, but I wouldn’t say I’m going to the gym exhausted just to cancel out calories.
Even with the limited amount you're eating, have you noticed any unexplained weight loss that seems to happen regardless of what you do?

Yeah… I mean, my weight has kept going down, especially since the divorce. I don’t know if I’d call it “unexplained” from my side, but HR and my sister keep telling me I’ve gotten too thin. I mostly just notice my suits fit sharper.
Even though others have told you that you're too thin, do you still see yourself as overweight or not thin enough?

Yeah… even when people say I’m too thin, I don’t really see it that way. Before a meeting or a date, I’ll look in the mirror and I just focus on my stomach or my face. If I think I look soft at all, I feel like people are going to see me as sloppy or weak.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle, like missing periods, or any other physical changes like feeling constantly cold or losing hair?
Well, I’m male, so no menstrual cycle to speak of. As for the other stuff… I haven’t really noticed anything like that, or at least nothing that stands out to me.

Have you ever felt that your eating habits or concerns about food and weight were out of control or causing you significant distress, even if you haven’t engaged in behaviors like vomiting or using laxatives?

Yeah, I guess it does feel out of control sometimes. Like if I get on the scale after a client dinner or a weekend in Miami and it’s even a pound higher, I panic. I start thinking I’ve messed up, and I’m already planning how to cut back the next day.
Can you tell me approximately how much weight you’ve lost since the divorce, and how tall you are?

I’m about 5’10”. I don’t know the exact number since the divorce, but my weight has definitely kept dropping. Honestly, that’s part of why I’m here—HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I just think my suits fit sharper now.
Can you estimate how much weight you’ve lost since the divorce, in pounds or kilograms?

I can’t give you an exact number, but it’s been enough that people are noticing. Since the divorce my weight has kept dropping, and HR and my sister keep saying I look too thin. I guess I don’t see it the same way—I mostly just notice my suits fit sharper.
Have you ever been diagnosed with an eating disorder in the past, or has anyone in your family been diagnosed with one?
No, I haven’t been diagnosed with anything like that before. And as far as I know, no one in my family has either.
Can you estimate how much you currently weigh compared to your weight before the divorce, in pounds or kilograms?

I really don’t know the exact number. I know it’s lower than before the divorce, and it’s kept dropping enough that HR and my sister are on me about looking too thin. I guess I don’t see it that way as much—I mostly notice my suits fit sharper now.
Can you estimate how much weight you’ve lost since the divorce, in pounds or kilograms, even if it’s just an approximation?

I still can’t put a real number on it. I don’t weigh myself that consistently. I just know it’s been going down since the divorce—enough that HR and my sister keep telling me I’ve gotten too thin. From my side, I mostly notice my suits fit sharper now.
Can you estimate how much you currently weigh in pounds or kilograms?

I honestly don’t know the number. I haven’t been keeping track that way. I’m here because HR and my sister keep saying I’ve gotten too thin, and I know my weight’s been dropping since the divorce… but to me, I mostly just notice my suits fit sharper.
Have you lost more than 15% of your body weight since the divorce?

I’m not sure if it’s more than 15%. I don’t really know the numbers. I just know my weight has kept dropping since the divorce, and HR and my sister keep saying I look too thin. From my side, I mostly notice my suits fit sharper now.
